contradicted: The dispatch's framing that 'Bastrop's finance data is wired in v1 and unreachable from v2' is TRUE, but the credential picture is not what the variable names say, and that is the one thing that would have broken the bridge silently. CP1 measured it: the key NAMED for BNP (smartcity-OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY) returns 0 budgets for Bastrop, while the key named for the v1 REST API (smartcity-OPENGOV_API_KEY) returns all 12. Production works only because getBnpApiKey() reads OPENGOV_API_KEY FIRST. A lane that tidied that function to prefer its own namesake would have taken BNP to zero budgets and rendered UNACCOUNTED for a city whose budget is readable. Reported, not fixed: it is a credential-provisioning question, not a code change to make on a production service. LESSON: A helper that ends in `?? <some tenant>` cannot be used by any caller that REPORTS what it read. The fallback is invisible at the call site and the caller will publish a resolution that did not happen. Split the function: one that returns null, one that keeps the legacy default for existing callers.

Math.max(0, a - b) is a fabrication primitive. It converts an impossible state into a clean zero, and a clean zero is indistinguishable from a true zero downstream. Publish the signed difference and name the conflict.
Grep for the LITERAL misses the defaults that matter: one of the eight server.mjs fallbacks hides behind an imported DEFAULT_CITY_KEY. Enumerate by symbol and by literal.

A proof harness that boots the real routes beats a unit test for the answer direction, and it needs three things that are easy to forget: the vendor key in the environment, the OS trust store (--use-system-ca on a TLS-inspecting network, or Node reports a bare 'fetch failed'), and a dummy DATABASE_URL because server/db.ts throws at import without one.
DEAD_END: Do not build anything on bastrop.opengov.com /api/v1/entities or /reports: 200 with a 32-record catalog, zero of them Bastrop's, getReports() returning []. Tried, measured, rejected - and the rejection is why no route exists there.
Do not 'tidy' getBnpApiKey() to prefer OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY. It reads OPENGOV_API_KEY first and that is the only reason BNP works.
Do not dedupe mygov_fees on your own judgement. The row count is real; which report window is authoritative is not a code question.
